mainTopic: Why one may not tithe one kind of produce to cover another: wine and grain, all other species, and the start of a challenge from מעשר בהמה.
overview: The גמרא already has a verse showing that you cannot tithe wine to cover oil. It asks how we know the same rule for wine and grain, or for two kinds of grain. It answers with a קל וחומר based on כלאים. That קל וחומר seems to fail according to רבי יאשיה's view of כלאים, so the גמרא rewords it to work for him too, using כלאים that happen 'through something else.' Next it asks about other species, like beans and lentils. It answers that their tithing is only דרבנן, and the רבנן made their rules match the Torah's rules. Finally, רבא בר רב חנן begins a challenge to אביי from מעשר בהמה, where the verse writes 'tithe' only once for both cattle and sheep. The challenge is completed on the next amud.

steps.title: We have a source for wine and oil, but what about grain?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא already has a source that wine and oil cannot be tithed one for the other. It asks for a source for wine with grain, and for one grain with another grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for wine and oil. From where do we know the rule for wine and grain, or for grain and grain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know that wine and grain, or two kinds of grain, cannot be tithed one for the other. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the rule was proven only for תירוש and יצהר. The גמרא now wants to extend the same rule to other pairs, and it needs a source for that.

phrases.english: We found a source for wine and oil;
phrases.notes: This means the rule that you cannot tithe from one for the other, which was proven earlier.

phrases.english: wine and grain,
or grain and a different grain: from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן תִּירוֹשׁ וְיִצְהָר, תִּירוֹשׁ וְדָגָן דָּגָן וְדָגָן מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the earlier source for wine and oil.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that wine with grain, and grain with grain, cannot be tithed one for the other.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from the laws of כלאים
steps.stepSummary: Wine and oil are not כלאים with each other, yet they cannot be tithed one for the other. Wine and grain, and two grains, are כלאים with each other, so they surely cannot be tithed one for the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn it with a קל וחומר. Wine and oil are not forbidden as mixed planting with each other, and still they cannot be tithed one for the other. Wine and grain, or grain and grain, are forbidden as mixed planting with each other. Isn't it logical that they cannot be tithed one for the other?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a קל וחומר. The argument is: pairs that are more 'separate' under the law of כלאים should surely not be tithed one for the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כלאים shows that the Torah treats these kinds as different from each other. Wine and oil are not even כלאים, yet they still cannot be tithed for each other. So pairs that are כלאים are even more 'separate' and certainly cannot be tithed for each other.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case (a fortiori)
Forbidden mixed planting of different species
Tithed from this one to cover that one

phrases.english: It is learned by an a fortiori argument:
If wine and oil,
which are not forbidden mixtures with each other,
still may not be tithed from one for the other,
then wine and grain, or grain and grain,
which are forbidden mixtures with each other,
is it not logical
that they may not be tithed from one for the other?

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from כלאים: pairs that are כלאים with each other surely cannot be tithed one for the other.

steps.title: This argument does not work for רבי יאשיה
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יאשיה, the Torah's כלאים of the vineyard applies only when wheat, barley, and a grape seed are sown together in one throw. Wine and grain are then not כלאים by themselves, so how does he learn the rule?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי יאשיה, who says a person is not liable until he sows wheat, barley, and a grape seed with one movement of the hand, how does he derive this rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the קל וחומר from step 2. For רבי יאשיה, its starting assumption is not true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed that wine and grain, or two grains, are כלאים as a pair. רבי יאשיה holds that the Torah's כלאים needs three kinds sown together. So for him, a pair alone is not כלאים, and the קל וחומר falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא with a strict definition of the Torah's כלאים of the vineyard
With a single throw (movement) of the hand

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יאשיה is not saying that wine and grain may be tithed for each other. He is only defining when Torah-level כלאים applies. Because of that definition, the proof needs to be rebuilt for his view.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yoshiya, who says:
one is not liable until he sows wheat, barley, and a grape seed
with a single movement of the hand,
how does he derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the starting assumption of the קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that wine and grain, or grain and grain, are כלאים with each other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי יאשיה, two kinds alone are not Torah-level כלאים, so the 'stricter' side of the קל וחומר is missing.

steps.title: Rebuilding the קל וחומר: כלאים 'through something else'
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי יאשיה agrees that wine and grain, or two grains, become כלאים when a third kind is added. Wine and oil never become כלאים, even with a third kind. So the קל וחומר still works.
steps.simpleTranslation: He derives it this way. Wine and oil are not forbidden mixtures with each other even when something else is added, and still they cannot be tithed one for the other. Wine and grain, or grain and grain, are forbidden mixtures with each other when something else is added. Isn't it logical that they cannot be tithed one for the other?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rewords the קל וחומר so that it fits רבי יאשיה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison no longer needs the pair to be כלאים by itself. It is enough that the pair can become כלאים when a third kind joins it. Wine and oil can never become כלאים at all. That is still a real difference, so the קל וחומר holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Through something else (when a third kind is added)

phrases.english: He derives it like this:
If wine and oil,
which are not forbidden mixtures with each other
even when something else is added,
still may not be tithed from one for the other,
then wine and grain, or grain and grain,
which are forbidden mixtures with each other
when something else is added,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא יִתְעַשְּׂרוּ מִזֶּה עַל זֶה?
phrases.english: is it not logical that they may not be tithed from one for the other?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by rewording the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reformulating the argument so that it fits the other view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר needed the pair to be כלאים by itself, which fails for רבי יאשיה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is enough that the pair becomes כלאים when a third kind is added, while wine and oil never do.

steps.title: What about other species in general?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that any two other species, like beans and lentils, cannot be tithed one for the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And two species in general: from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about species other than grain, wine, and oil. It is setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר covered only דגן, תירוש, and יצהר, the kinds the Torah names. Other produce is not covered by it, so a new source is needed.

phrases.english: And two species in general: from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the Torah-named kinds to all other species.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that species other than grain, wine, and oil cannot be tithed one for the other.

steps.title: Rabbinic tithes follow the Torah's pattern
steps.stepSummary: Tithing other species is only דרבנן. The רבנן made their rules like Torah rules, so here too two species cannot be tithed one for the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are only rabbinic. Everything the רבנן enacted, they enacted like Torah law. Just as under Torah law two species cannot be tithed one for the other, so too under rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these species are tithed only מדרבנן, and the רבנן copied the Torah's rule for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No verse is needed here, because the obligation itself is rabbinic. A general principle applies instead: the רבנן shaped their enactments on the Torah's model, so they included the Torah's rule against tithing one species for another.

keyTerms.term: כֹּל דְּתַקִּינוּ רַבָּנַן כְּעֵין דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא תַּקִּינוּ
keyTerms.meaning: Whatever the רבנן enacted, they enacted it like Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: Wine and oil: learned from a verse. Wine and grain, and grain and grain: learned from a קל וחומר based on כלאים, which also works for רבי יאשיה through 'something else.' All other species: tithed only מדרבנן, and the same rule applies because the רבנן followed the Torah's model.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle כל דתקון רבנן כעין דאורייתא תקון appears all across ש״ס. It explains why rabbinic laws copy the details of the Torah laws they are modeled on.

phrases.english: These are tithed only by rabbinic law,
and everything that the Sages enacted,
they enacted it like Torah law:
just as under Torah law two species
may not be tithed from one for the other,
so too under rabbinic law.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Other species are tithed מדרבנן, and the רבנן modeled their enactments on Torah law, so the same rule applies.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: No two species may be tithed one for the other, whether the obligation comes from the Torah or from the רבנן.

steps.title: רבא בר רב חנן begins a challenge from מעשר בהמה
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנן challenges אביי by pointing to the verse of מעשר בהמה. There, the word 'tithe' is not written separately for cattle and for sheep.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב חנן said to אביי: If so, then with מעשר בהמה, where the Torah does not write 'and all the tithe of the herd and the tithe of the flock' (it only says 'tithe' once for both)...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר רב חנן is starting a challenge against אביי by pointing to the verse of מעשר בהמה. This line only sets up the problem; the actual question comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה' mean 'if your reasoning is right, then look what follows.' רבא בר רב חנן notes that the verse says 'מעשר בקר וצאן,' with the word 'tithe' written only once for both cattle and sheep. Read with אביי's approach, that wording seems to lead to a problem that the next passage will spell out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so, then...' This phrase opens a challenge by drawing a problematic result from someone's reasoning.
Animal tithe: every tenth animal of the herd or flock is set aside as holy.
'Where it is not written.' The argument is built on what the verse does NOT say.

steps.confusionAlert: The verse quoted here, 'וְכׇל מַעְשַׂר בָּקָר וּמַעֲשֵׂר צֹאן,' is NOT the real פסוק. It is a made-up version showing how the Torah could have written it, with 'tithe' said twice. The real verse (ויקרא כז:לב) says 'tithe' only once for both cattle and sheep. That difference is the whole point of the challenge.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Chanan said to Abaye:
If that is so,
phrases.notes: A standard opening for a challenge: 'if your logic holds, then...'

phrases.english: then regarding animal tithe,
where it is not written
phrases.notes: The argument depends on what the Torah did NOT write.

phrases.english: "And all the tithe of the herd and the tithe of the flock"
phrases.notes: A hypothetical wording, with 'tithe' said twice. The actual verse (ויקרא כז:לב) says 'tithe' only once for both.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the verse-based source for wine and oil mentioned in step 1, and challenges it by comparing it to the wording of the מעשר בהמה verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier derivation (referred to in step 1) that wine and oil may not be tithed one for the other because the verse mentions each one separately.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In מעשר בהמה, the word 'tithe' is written only once for both cattle and sheep. Under אביי's reasoning this seems to produce an unwanted result, which will be stated on the next amud.
